question: We have two tests to diagnose a serious prognosis disease. Test A has a sensitivity of 95% and a specificity of 60% and test B has a sensitivity of 70% and a specificity of 99%. We have an effective treatment but that produces important adverse effects and also has a very high cost. What test would we choose to make the diagnosis?

options.opa: Test A because it will detect less false positives.
options.opb: Test A because it has a higher sensitivity.
options.opc: Test B because it will detect more false positives.
options.opd: Test A because it will detect more false negatives.
options.ope: Test B because it has a greater specificity.

analysis: When deciding between Test A and Test B for diagnosing a serious prognosis disease, it is crucial to consider both sensitivity and specificity. Sensitivity is the ability of a test to correctly identify those with the disease, while specificity is the ability of a test to correctly identify those without the disease. In this case, Test B has a higher specificity (99%) compared to Test A (60%). Given that the disease is serious and the treatment has important adverse effects and high cost, it is important to minimize false positives to avoid unnecessary treatment. Therefore, Test B with higher specificity would be the preferred choice in this scenario.
